question_gloss: Whether certain words will continue to be used or remain in language.

rotation.source_passage:
Where you found them at?
Got 'em 'round town, could've drowned in it
Would have floated, boated, voted
Sugar-coated, loaded hip shooter
Draw for the poor, free coffee at the banks
Yip through the straw, none more for me, thanks
That blanks the raw, that dank sure stank lit
Sank past the pit for more hardcore prank spit
Crank it on blast, roll past Front Street
Blew the whole spot like some old ass with skunk meat
These kids is too fast, juiced off a junk treat
Who could get looser off a crunk or a funk beat?
rotation.enantiomorph:
Where you ignited them at?
Got 'em across the kindling, could've immolated in it
Would have risen, ferried, sworn
Pitch-lacquered, primed flint striker
Spark for the scorched, molten tar at the furnaces
Hiss through the wick, all of me now, burning
That chars the nerve, that sulfur sure smoldered lit
Caved past the crater for more white-hot tongue-fire
Stoke it on blast, scorch through Front Street
Razed the whole block like some spent coal with brimstone
These embers is too bright, fueled off a phosphor ration
Who could get more consumed off a conflagration or a furnace pulse?

rite.speaker: Johannes Sigil
rite.text: The rite opens over something that has been moving at street-level, moving fast, compressing a whole world of transaction — the sugar, the drawl, the shooter, the bank, the beat — into a velocity that is itself the argument. The question the witness brings is whether these words go on, which is the oldest question, the one Sappho asked in a burning room, the one the psalmist asked at the edge of Babylon. What the first operator will traverse in them is the axis of cost: what it bore to say this at this speed, at this pitch, with this much of the world packed into a single breath — and what of that bearing survives when the voice stops. I am naming the threshold. I am handing you to Rebekah Cranes.
